papers.title: On the 50th year responding to Ebola: mapping diagnostic, vaccine, and therapeutic gaps across ebolavirus species
papers.abstract: This year marks the 50th anniversary of the Ebola virus identification, but the 2026 outbreak of Bundibugyo ebolavirus disease has exposed important limitations in Ebola preparedness strategies that remain largely focused on Zaire ebolavirus. Although major advances in diagnostics, vaccines, and therapeutics have followed the 2014-2016 West African Ebola epidemic, most licensed countermeasures were developed against Zaire ebolavirus and may provide limited protection against other ebolavirus species, including Bundibugyo ebolavirus. Herein, we examine the epidemiological significance of Bundibugyo ebolavirus and review current and emerging diagnostics, vaccines, antibody therapies, and antiviral strategies, with emphasis on their species coverage and limitations. We further discuss how diagnostic blind spots and limited species-inclusive countermeasures contributed to challenges during the current outbreak. Future Ebola preparedness should adopt a broader framework encompassing multiple ebolavirus species with epidemic potential.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 自 2014 年至 2016 年西非埃博拉疫情以来,诊断、疫苗 和治疗方面取得了重大进展,但大多数获得许可的对策是针对扎伊尔埃博拉病毒制定的,并且可能对其他埃博拉病毒物种(包括本迪布焦埃博拉病毒)提供有限的保护。

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的埃博拉防范工作应采用更广泛的框架,涵盖具有流行潜力的多种埃博拉病毒物种,以解决诊断和对策方面的差距。

papers.title: Ebola virus disease in the modern era: pathogenesis, therapeutic advances, vaccine strategies, and global health preparedness
papers.abstract: Ebola virus disease (EVD) remains one of the most severe and complex viral hemorrhagic fevers confronting global public health systems. Since its first recognized emergence in 1976, recurrent outbreaks caused primarily by Zaire ebolavirus have demonstrated the extraordinary epidemic potential of filoviruses, particularly in regions with fragile healthcare infrastructure. The unprecedented West African epidemic of 2013-2016 fundamentally altered scientific understanding of Ebola virus transmission, pathogenesis, clinical progression, and outbreak management. Subsequent outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda have further emphasized the persistent risk posed by Ebola virus disease despite advances in diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccination strategies. Ebola virus infection is characterized by extensive immune dysregulation, aberrant inflammatory responses, endothelial dysfunction, coagulopathy, and progressive multiorgan injury. Recent studies have significantly expanded understanding of viral persistence, post-Ebola syndrome, host immune responses, and mechanisms of viral immune evasion. Parallel developments in molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, monoclonal antibody therapy, and recombinant vaccine platforms have substantially improved survival outcomes and epidemic control measures. Although India has not experienced endemic Ebola outbreaks, globalization and increasing international mobility have heightened the possibility of imported infections, necessitating robust preparedness frameworks. Following the West African epidemic, India strengthened airport surveillance, laboratory biosafety capacity, integrated disease surveillance systems, and emergency outbreak-response protocols. However, substantial challenges remain regarding rapid diagnostics, healthcare infrastructure, biosafety training, and public awareness. This review critically examines current advances in Ebola virus epidemiology, molecular biology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnostics, therapeutics, vaccine development, and public health preparedness, with particular emphasis on implications for India and future global health security.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the current state of knowledge on Ebola virus disease (EVD), focusing on its pathogenesis, therapeutic advances, vaccine strategies, and global health preparedness. It highlights the epidemic potential of Zaire ebolavirus, particularly in regions with weak healthcare systems, and discusses the impact of the 2013-2016 West African outbreak on scientific understanding. The review emphasizes immune dysregulation, inflammatory responses, and multiorgan injury as key features of EVD. It also addresses the challenges in diagnostics, infrastructure, and public awareness, while noting the progress in molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, monoclonal antibody therapy, and vaccine development. The implications for India, including the need for robust preparedness frameworks and strengthened surveillance systems, are underscored due to the risk of imported infections. The review serves as a critical analysis of advances and ongoing challenges in managing EVD and enhancing global health security.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 埃博拉病毒病 (EVD) 仍然是全球公共卫生系统面临的最严重、最复杂的病毒性出血热之一。这篇综述批判性地审视了 埃博拉病毒 流行病学、分子生物学、发病机制、临床表现、诊断、治疗、疫苗 开发和公共卫生准备方面的当前进展,特别强调对印度和未来全球卫生安全的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 自 1976 年首次出现以来,主要由扎伊尔埃博拉病毒引起的反复出现的 暴发 已经证明了丝状病毒具有非凡的流行潜力,特别是在医疗基础设施脆弱的地区。2013-2016 年前所未有的西非疫情从根本上改变了对 埃博拉病毒、传播、发病机制、临床进展和 暴发 管理的科学认识。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 埃博拉病毒 感染的特点是广泛的免疫失调、异常的炎症反应、内皮功能障碍、凝血障碍和进行性多器官损伤。最近的研究显着扩展了对病毒持久性、埃博拉后综合征、宿主 免疫应答 和病毒免疫逃避机制的理解。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 在快速诊断、医疗基础设施、生物安全培训和公众意识方面仍然存在巨大挑战。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 分子诊断、基因组监测、单克隆抗体疗法和重组疫苗平台的并行发展大大改善了生存结果和流行病控制措施。尽管印度没有经历过埃博拉疫情 暴发,但全球化和不断增加的国际流动性增加了输入性感染的可能性,因此需要强有力的防备框架。西非疫情爆发后,印度加强了机场 监测、实验室生物安全能力、综合疾病 监测 系统和紧急 暴发 响应方案。

papers.title_zh: 现代的 埃博拉病毒病:发病机制、治疗进展、疫苗 策略和全球健康准备
papers.source_body_en: Ebola virus disease (EVD) remains one of the most severe and complex viral hemorrhagic fevers confronting global public health systems. Since its first recognized emergence in 1976, recurrent outbreaks caused primarily by Zaire ebolavirus have demonstrated the extraordinary epidemic potential of filoviruses, particularly in regions with fragile healthcare infrastructure. The unprecedented West African epidemic of 2013-2016 fundamentally altered scientific understanding of Ebola virus transmission, pathogenesis, clinical progression, and outbreak management. Subsequent outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda have further emphasized the persistent risk posed by Ebola virus disease despite advances in diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccination strategies. Ebola virus infection is characterized by extensive immune dysregulation, aberrant inflammatory responses, endothelial dysfunction, coagulopathy, and progressive multiorgan injury. Recent studies have significantly expanded understanding of viral persistence, post-Ebola syndrome, host immune responses, and mechanisms of viral immune evasion. Parallel developments in molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, monoclonal antibody therapy, and recombinant vaccine platforms have substantially improved survival outcomes and epidemic control measures. Although India has not experienced endemic Ebola outbreaks, globalization and increasing international mobility have heightened the possibility of imported infections, necessitating robust preparedness frameworks. Following the West African epidemic, India strengthened airport surveillance, laboratory biosafety capacity, integrated disease surveillance systems, and emergency outbreak-response protocols. However, substantial challenges remain regarding rapid diagnostics, healthcare infrastructure, biosafety training, and public awareness. This review critically examines current advances in Ebola virus epidemiology, molecular biology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnostics, therapeutics, vaccine development, and public health preparedness, with particular emphasis on implications for India and future global health security.

papers.title: Cross-Border Ebola Virus Disease Preparedness in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo: A Systematic Review of Health Security Capacities, Gaps, and Priorities
papers.abstract: Background: Recurrent Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continue to pose substantial cross-border health security risks to neighbouring countries, particularly Uganda. Although numerous preparedness initiatives have been implemented to prevent, detect, and respond to cross-border Ebola transmission, evidence on their effectiveness, strengths, and persistent gaps remains fragmented across peer-reviewed and grey-literature sources. This review synthesized available evidence on cross-border Ebola preparedness in Uganda and the DRC and identified key capacities, challenges, and priorities for strengthening regional health security. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and reported using the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) framework. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, African Journals Online (AJOL), and major grey-literature sources were searched from January 2000 to 18 May 2026. Findings were synthesized across nine predefined preparedness domains. Results Seventy-one evidence sources were included, comprising 32 primary studies and 39 grey-literature documents. Evidence was most concentrated in border surveillance and point-of-entry preparedness (24 sources), contact tracing and rapid response (22 sources), cross-border mobility and importation risk (18 sources), infection prevention and control (17 sources), and regional governance and coordination (17 sources). Preparedness activities included mobility mapping, traveller screening, healthcare-worker training, laboratory strengthening, risk communication, and cross-border coordination mechanisms. The synthesis identified substantial preparedness capacity across surveillance systems, laboratory readiness, healthcare-facility preparedness, and regional collaboration. However, important gaps persisted in some major preparedness domains. Conclusions Cross-border Ebola preparedness in Uganda and the DRC has expanded considerably over the past two decades through investments in surveillance systems, laboratory networks, healthcare-worker preparedness, and regional coordination. Nonetheless, persistent vulnerabilities remain in humanitarian settings, preparedness sustainability, and emerging preparedness domains. Strengthening integrated, sustainable, and cross-border health-security systems will be critical for mitigating future Ebola threats and enhancing epidemic preparedness across East Africa.

source_records.abstract: Background Recurrent Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continue to pose substantial cross-border health security risks to neighbouring countries, particularly Uganda. Although numerous preparedness initiatives have been implemented to prevent, detect, and respond to cross-border Ebola transmission, evidence on their effectiveness, strengths, and persistent gaps remains fragmented across peer-reviewed and grey-literature sources. This review synthesized available evidence on cross-border Ebola preparedness in Uganda and the DRC and identified key capacities, challenges, and priorities for strengthening regional health security. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and reported using the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) framework. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, African Journals Online (AJOL), and major grey-literature sources were searched from January 2000 to 18 May 2026. Findings were synthesized across nine predefined preparedness domains. Results Seventy-one evidence sources were included, comprising 32 primary studies and 39 grey-literature documents. Evidence was most concentrated in border surveillance and point-of-entry preparedness (24 sources), contact tracing and rapid response (22 sources), cross-border mobility and importation risk (18 sources), infection prevention and control (17 sources), and regional governance and coordination (17 sources). Preparedness activities included mobility mapping, traveller screening, healthcare-worker training, laboratory strengthening, risk communication, and cross-border coordination mechanisms. The synthesis identified substantial preparedness capacity across surveillance systems, laboratory readiness, healthcare-facility preparedness, and regional collaboration. However, important gaps persisted in some major preparedness domains. Conclusions Cross-border Ebola preparedness in Uganda and the DRC has expanded considerably over the past two decades through investments in surveillance systems, laboratory networks, healthcare-worker preparedness, and regional coordination. Nonetheless, persistent vulnerabilities remain in humanitarian settings, preparedness sustainability, and emerging preparedness domains. Strengthening integrated, sustainable, and cross-border health-security systems will be critical for mitigating future Ebola threats and enhancing epidemic preparedness across East Africa.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:刚果民主共和国(DRC)经常发生的 埃博拉病毒病 (EVD) 暴发 继续对邻国(特别是乌干达)构成重大跨境卫生安全风险。尽管已经实施了许多准备举措来预防、检测和应对跨境埃博拉 传播,但有关其有效性、优势和持续差距的证据在同行评审和灰色文献来源中仍然支离破碎。本次审查综合了乌干达和刚果民主共和国跨境埃博拉防范工作的现有证据,并确定了加强区域卫生安全的关键能力、挑战和优先事项。方法 根据 PRISMA 2020 进行系统评价,并使用无荟萃分析综合 (SWiM) 框架进行报告。从 2000 年 1 月到 2026 年 5 月 18 日,我们对 PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science、非洲在线期刊 (AJOL) 和主要灰色文献来源进行了检索。结果综合了九个预定义的准备领域。结果 纳入 71 个证据来源,其中包括 32 项初步研究和 39 份灰色文献。证据主要集中在边境 监测 和入境点准备(24 个来源)、接触者追踪和快速反应(22 个来源)、跨境流动和输入风险(18 个来源)、感染预防和控制(17 个来源)以及区域治理和协调(17 个来源)。准备活动包括流动测绘、旅行者筛查、医护人员培训、实验室强化、风险沟通和跨境协调机制。该综合报告确定了 监测 系统、实验室准备、医疗设施准备和区域合作的大​​量准备能力。然而,一些主要的准备领​​域仍然存在重大差距。结论 过去二十年来,通过对 监测 系统、实验室网络、医护人员准备和区域协调的投资,乌干达和刚果民主共和国的跨境埃博拉准备工作大幅扩展。尽管如此,人道主义环境、备灾可持续性和新兴备灾领域仍然存在持续的脆弱性。加强综合、可持续和跨境卫生安全系统对于减轻未来的埃博拉威胁和加强整个东非的流行病防范至关重要。

papers.title: Ebola virus disease at the human–animal–environment interface: a scoping review of recent outbreaks, transmission dynamics, and future preventive strategies
papers.abstract: Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) remains among the most lethal zoonotic hemorrhagic fevers, with case fatality rates (CFRs) of 25% to over 90%. Since 2018, successive major outbreaks; the 10th Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) epidemic (2018–2020), the 2021 Guinea resurgence, the Uganda Sudan ebolavirus outbreaks (2022, 2025), the 16th DRC (Kasai) outbreak (2025), and the 2026 Bundibugyo virus emergency declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern have claimed thousands of lives, underscoring EVD’s persistent threat at the human–animal–environment interface and critical preparedness gaps. This scoping review synthesizes recent evidence on EVD outbreak dynamics, zoonotic transmission, genomic epidemiology, therapeutic and vaccine developments, and the sociocultural and ecological drivers of outbreaks. Following PRISMA-ScR, we searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (inception to May 2026), supplemented by WHO outbreak reports. Fifty eligible sources were included, over 90% published 2018–2026. The DRC 10th outbreak (3,470 cases; CFR 66.2%) was exacerbated by armed conflict, nosocomial transmission, and community resistance. The 2021 Guinea resurgence was genetically linked to a 2014–2016 survivor, revealing viral persistence in immune-privileged tissues. The 2022 Uganda outbreak (164 cases; CFR 46.3%) highlighted super-spreading and inadequate infection control at private facilities. Frugivorous Pteropodidae bats remain the likely reservoir. Approved monoclonal antibodies Inmazeb and Ebanga showed 28-day mortality of 33.5% and 35.1% versus 49.7% for ZMapp; rVSV-ZEBOV protects against Zaire but not Sudan ebolavirus. Recent events reinforced these themes: 2025 Uganda (14 cases; CFR 29%) saw the first SUDV ring-vaccination trial; 2025 DRC-Kasai (64 cases; CFR 70.3%) was contained within ~ 3 months; and 2026 Bundibugyo again exposed absent countermeasures for non-Zaire species. Integrated One Health surveillance, equitable therapeutic and vaccine access, community engagement, and genomic epidemiology must anchor future EVD prevention. Urgent investment in Sudan ebolavirus vaccines and outbreak-resilient health systems is essential. This is the first comprehensive scoping review to integrate evidence from all three major post-2018 EVD outbreaks namely the DRC 10th epidemic, the 2021 Guinea resurgence, and the 2022 Uganda Sudan ebolavirus outbreak within a unified One Health framework. We provide a novel synthesis of genomic epidemiology alongside clinical, ecological, and sociocultural transmission determinants, bridging the gap between laboratory science and public health practice. The review critically appraises FDA-approved therapeutics (Inmazeb, Ebanga) and vaccine strategies (rVSV-ZEBOV) within the context of ongoing outbreaks caused by non-Zaire ebolaviruses for which no approved medical countermeasures currently exist. Our analysis highlights the paradigm-shifting finding that EVD can re-emerge years after an epidemic through persistence of Zaire ebolavirus in survivor immune-privileged tissues, with direct implications for long-term surveillance policies.

papers.title: ESM-embedR: a protein language model framework for comparative mutation analysis and computational atypicality scoring of Lassa and Ebola virus sequences
papers.abstract: The emergence and re-emergence of viral pathogens with pandemic potential necessitate robust computational frameworks capable of interpreting sequence variation in evolutionary and functional contexts. Lassa virus (LASV) and Ebola virus (EBOV), two members of the Arenaviridae and Filoviridae families, respectively, represent contrasting evolutionary paradigms: LASV exhibits substantial genetic diversity across West Africa, while EBOV outbreaks have historically been characterised by more constrained genetic variation. Understanding the differential mutational constraints governing these viruses provides critical insights for surveillance, vaccine design, and therapeutic development. This study presents a comprehensive, end-to-end computational framework bridging comparative virology and practical deployment. Analysis encompassed 2,502 glycoprotein (GP) sequences (780 LASV GP, 1722 EBOV GP) sourced from NCBI GenBank across all documented EBOV outbreaks (1976–2024) and curated LASV repositories. EBOV GP was extracted from full-genome assemblies via reference-guided alignment (MAFFT), enabling a direct, protein-scope-matched comparison. The framework integrates MAFFT-aligned site-level constraint categorisation through conservation and entropy analysis with substitution burden quantification to characterise the mutational landscape. Protein language model embedding-space characterisation using ESM-2 provides complementary descriptive insight through centroid geometry, outlier detection, and PCA visualisation. For supervised classification and deployment, the framework employs lightweight, interpretable composition features (sequence length and amino-acid frequencies) rather than ESM-2 embeddings, an intentional design choice that prioritises deployment efficiency and interpretability. The classifier is coupled with a computational atypicality scoring layer that quantifies sequence deviation from training-population centroids. The comparative analysis revealed profound asymmetries in mutational architecture. EBOV GP exhibited near-complete positional constraint with 94.7% of aligned sites classified as Critical and 5.3% as Conserved, while LASV GP displayed substantial flexibility with 92.0% Hotspots, 5.3% Intermediate sites, 2.2% Conserved, and 0.5% Critical. ESM-2 embedding analysis corroborated these findings. A logistic regression classifier achieved perfect held-out performance (accuracy 1.000, precision 1.000, recall 1.000, F1 1.000, ROC-AUC 1.000) on the GP-matched cohort, reflecting robust class separability while acknowledging that this performance cannot be assumed to generalise to all independent EBOV or LASV variants without explicit validation. This model was integrated with an interpretable atypicality layer generating a computational atypicality index with bounded interpretive bands, atypicality z-scores, and natural language interpretations, deployed via a public Streamlit application. The novelty of this work lies in the integration of established methods (site-level constraint analysis, substitution-burden quantification, protein language model embedding characterization, interpretable classification, and atypicality scoring) into a single reproducible, openly deployable pipeline for comparative LASV-EBOV sequence analysis. Each individual method has precedents in isolation; their synthesis within a unified framework that transforms static comparative insights into dynamic, accessible sequence-analysis capabilities represents the principal advance.

Lassa virus (LASV) and Ebola virus (EBOV), two members of the Arenaviridae and Filoviridae families, respectively, represent contrasting evolutionary paradigms: LASV exhibits substantial genetic diversity across West Africa, while EBOV outbreaks have historically been characterised by more constrained genetic variation. Understanding the differential mutational constraints governing these viruses provides critical insights for surveillance, vaccine design, and therapeutic development. This study presents a comprehensive, end-to-end computational framework bridging comparative virology and practical deployment. Analysis encompassed 2,502 glycoprotein (GP) sequences (780 LASV GP, 1722 EBOV GP) sourced from NCBI GenBank across all documented EBOV outbreaks (1976–2024) and curated LASV repositories. EBOV GP was extracted from full-genome assemblies via reference-guided alignment (MAFFT), enabling a direct, protein-scope-matched comparison. The framework integrates MAFFT-aligned site-level constraint categorisation through conservation and entropy analysis with substitution burden quantification to characterise the mutational landscape. Protein language model embedding-space characterisation using ESM-2 provides complementary descriptive insight through centroid geometry, outlier detection, and PCA visualisation. For supervised classification and deployment, the framework employs lightweight, interpretable composition features (sequence length and amino-acid frequencies) rather than ESM-2 embeddings, an intentional design choice that prioritises deployment efficiency and interpretability. The classifier is coupled with a computational atypicality scoring layer that quantifies sequence deviation from training-population centroids. The comparative analysis revealed profound asymmetries in mutational architecture. EBOV GP exhibited near-complete positional constraint with 94.7% of aligned sites classified as Critical and 5.3% as Conserved, while LASV GP displayed substantial flexibility with 92.0% Hotspots, 5.3% Intermediate sites, 2.2% Conserved, and 0.5% Critical. ESM-2 embedding analysis corroborated these findings. A logistic regression classifier achieved perfect held-out performance (accuracy 1.000, precision 1.000, recall 1.000, F1 1.000, ROC-AUC 1.000) on the GP-matched cohort, reflecting robust class separability while acknowledging that this performance cannot be assumed to generalise to all independent EBOV or LASV variants without explicit validation. This model was integrated with an interpretable atypicality layer generating a computational atypicality index with bounded interpretive bands, atypicality z-scores, and natural language interpretations, deployed via a public Streamlit application. The novelty of this work lies in the integration of established methods (site-level constraint analysis, substitution-burden quantification, protein language model embedding characterization, interpretable classification, and atypicality scoring) into a single reproducible, openly deployable pipeline for comparative LASV-EBOV sequence analysis. Each individual method has precedents in isolation; their synthesis within a unified framework that transforms static comparative insights into dynamic, accessible sequence-analysis capabilities represents the principal advance.

papers.abstract_zh: 具有大流行潜力的病毒病原体的出现和重新出现需要强大的计算框架,能够解释进化和功能环境中的序列变异。拉沙病毒 (LASV) 和 埃博拉病毒 (EBOV) 分别是沙粒病毒科和丝状病毒科的两个成员,代表着截然不同的进化范式:LASV 在整个西非表现出巨大的遗传多样性,而 EBOV 暴发 历史上的遗传变异更为有限。了解控制这些病毒的差异突变限制为 监测、疫苗 设计和治疗开发提供了重要的见解。这项研究提出了一个全面的、端到端的计算框架,将比较病毒学和实际部署联系起来。分析涵盖 2,502 个糖蛋白 (GP) 序列(780 个 LASV GP、1722 个 EBOV GP),这些序列源自 NCBI GenBank,涵盖所有记录的 EBOV 暴发 (1976-2024) 和精选的 LASV 存储库。通过参考引导比对 (MAFFT) 从完整的 基因组 组件中提取 EBOV GP,从而实现直接的蛋白质范围匹配比较。该框架通过保护和熵分析与替代负担量化整合了与 MAFFT 一致的位点级约束分类,以表征突变景观。使用 ESM-2 的蛋白质语言模型嵌入空间表征通过质心几何、异常值检测和 PCA 可视化提供补充的描述性见解。对于监督分类和部署,该框架采用轻量级、可解释的组成特征(序列长度和氨基酸频率)而不是 ESM-2 嵌入,这是一种优先考虑部署效率和可解释性的有意设计选择。该分类器与计算非典型性评分层相结合,该层可量化与训练群体质心的序列偏差。比较分析揭示了突变结构中深刻的不对称性。EBOV GP 表现出近乎完全的位置限制,其中 94.7% 的比对位点被分类为关键位点,5.3% 被分类为保守位点,而 LASV GP 显示出极大的灵活性,其中 92.0% 为热点位点,5.3% 为中间位点,2.2% 为保守位点,0.5% 为关键位点。ESM-2 嵌入分析证实了这些发现。逻辑回归分类器在 GP 匹配的 队列研究 上实现了完美的保留性能(准确率 1.000、精度 1.000、召回率 1.000、F1 1.000、ROC-AUC 1.000),反映了强大的类可分离性,同时承认在没有明确验证的情况下不能假设这种性能推广到所有独立的 EBOV 或 LASV 变体。该模型与可解释的非典型性层集成,生成具有有限解释带、非典型性 z 分数和自然语言解释的计算非典型性指数,通过公共 Streamlit 应用程序部署。这项工作的新颖性在于将已建立的方法(位点级约束分析、替代负担量化、蛋白质语言模型嵌入表征、可解释分类和非典型性评分)集成到单个可重复、可公开部署的管道中,用于比较 LASV-EBOV 序列分析。每种方法都有单独的先例;它们在一个统一的框架内进行综合,将静态的比较见解转化为动态的、可访问的序列分析能力,这代表了主要的进步。

analysis_zh.main_results: EBOV GP 表现出近乎完全的位置限制,其中 94.7% 的比对位点被分类为关键位点,5.3% 被分类为保守位点,而 LASV GP 显示出极大的灵活性,其中 92.0% 为热点位点,5.3% 为中间位点,2.2% 为保守位点,0.5% 为关键位点。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 EBOV 和 LASV 突变结构中深刻的不对称性解释为差异进化限制的证据,新颖之处在于将现有方法整合到一个统一的、可重复的管道中以进行比较序列分析。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以通过强调 EBOV 和 LASV 的对比突变景观,特别是 EBOV GP 的受限 进化,为 监测 策略和 疫苗 或治疗设计提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认,在没有明确验证的情况下,完美的分类器性能(准确度 1.000、精确度 1.000、召回率 1.000、F1 1.000、ROC-AUC 1.000)可能无法推广到所有独立的 EBOV 或 LASV 变体,这表明证据强度中等。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study highlights the increased risk of a Bundibugyo virus epidemic due to underinvestment in diagnostic and vaccine research and development. The authors argue that this lack of investment has hindered effective public health responses to the outbreak.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is an editorial analysis of the Bundibugyo virus epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda, focusing on the public health emergency declared by the World Health Organization on 16 May 2026. It examines the broader implications of underinvestment in diagnostic and vaccine research for managing such outbreaks.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a review of the public health emergency declaration and an analysis of the global response to the Bundibugyo virus outbreak, emphasizing the lack of investment in diagnostic and vaccine research as the central focus.
analysis.main_results: The main results indicate that the Bundibugyo virus outbreak was declared a public health emergency by the World Health Organization on 16 May 2026, underscoring the severity and potential global impact of the epidemic.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence of the critical need for increased investment in diagnostic and vaccine research for Ebola viruses, particularly Bundibugyo virus, to prevent future epidemics. This is a novel call to action for global health policy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have significant implications for public health policy, emphasizing the importance of prioritizing diagnostic and vaccine research for Bundibugyo virus to mitigate future outbreaks and improve global preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a single source, the World Health Organization's declaration, and does not include detailed statistical or experimental data. However, the evidence is strong given the official recognition of the public health emergency.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial discusses the 2026 Bundibugyo virus epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda, which was declared a public health emergency by the World Health Organization. The study emphasizes the role of underinvestment in diagnostic and vaccine research and development in exacerbating the risk of such outbreaks. It calls for increased global attention and resources to address these gaps, highlighting the potential consequences of neglecting research for Ebola viruses. The findings suggest that without targeted investment, future epidemics may be more severe and harder to control. The study's strength lies in its reference to an official declaration, but its limitations include the lack of detailed statistical or experimental data to support its claims.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究强调,由于诊断和 疫苗 研发投资不足,本迪布焦病毒流行的风险增加。作者认为,缺乏投资阻碍了对 暴发 的有效公共卫生反应。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对刚果民主共和国和乌干达本迪布焦病毒流行的编辑分析,重点关注世界卫生组织于 2026 年 5 月 16 日宣布的公共卫生紧急状态。它探讨了诊断和 疫苗 研究投资不足对管理此类 暴发 的更广泛影响。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法包括审查公共卫生紧急状态声明和分析全球对本迪布焦病毒 暴发 的反应,强调诊断和 疫苗 研究投资的缺乏是核心焦点。
elements_zh.main_results: 主要结果表明,世界卫生组织于2026年5月16日宣布本迪布焦病毒暴发为突发公共卫生事件,凸显了该流行病的严重性和潜在的全球影响。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明迫切需要增加对 埃博拉病毒(特别是本迪布焦病毒)的诊断和 疫苗 研究的投资,以预防未来的流行病。这是对全球卫生政策采取行动的新颖呼吁。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对公共卫生政策具有重大影响,强调优先考虑本迪布焦病毒的诊断和 疫苗 研究的重要性,以减轻未来的 疫苗 影响并提高全球防范能力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于单一来源,即世界卫生组织的声明,不包括详细的统计或实验数据。然而,鉴于官方承认公共卫生紧急情况,证据很充分。

papers.title: Safety and immunogenicity of one or two doses of the rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP Ebola virus vaccine in adults and adolescents living with HIV: a phase 2, multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: A single dose of the replication-competent rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccine is recommended by the WHO Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization during Ebola virus disease outbreaks. We aimed to assess the immunogenicity, safety, and tolerability of this vaccine in adults and adolescents with HIV. METHODS: In this phase 2, multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial, we enrolled participants aged 13-70 years who had laboratory-confirmed HIV infection, were on antiretroviral therapy (ART), had an undetectable viral load ( 350 and <500 cells per μL), cohort 3 (adults with a CD4 count of 200-350 cells per μL), cohort 4 (adolescents [age 13-17 years] with a CD4 count ≥200 cells per μL), and cohort 5 (adults and adolescents with a CD4 count ≥200 cells per μL). Participants were randomly assigned 4:1 to receive one dose (cohorts 1-4) or two doses (56 days apart; cohort 5) of rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP or placebo, administered at day 0. An unmasked staff member at each site prepared the vaccine or placebo; all other study personnel and participants were masked to group assignments. Participants were followed up to day 365. The primary immunogenicity endpoints, assessed in the per-protocol population, were Ebola virus-specific antibody responses measured by glycoprotein ELISA (GP-ELISA; geometric mean titre ratio [GMTR]) and neutralisation (geometric mean fold increase [GMFI] of plaque reduction neutralisation test [PRNT]) on day 28 in cohorts 1-5 combined (combined cohort), and 28 days after the second dose of vaccine or placebo in cohort 5. The primary safety endpoints, assessed in the as-treated population, were: the occurrence of each solicited local and systemic adverse event during a 14-day follow-up period after each vaccination; fever, joint pain (arthralgia), joint swelling (arthritis), rash, and blisters or vesicular lesions during a 42-day follow-up period after vaccination; any haematological and biochemical laboratory abnormality at 0, 3, 7, 14, and 28 days after each vaccine; occurrence of any unsolicited adverse event during a 42-day follow-up period after each vaccination; and occurrence of vaccine-related serious adverse events up to day 365 of the study. The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03031912) and is complete. FINDINGS: Between Aug 1, 2017, and March 3, 2022, we assessed 647 individuals for eligibility, 251 of whom were enrolled. 120 (48%) participants were male, 130 (52%) were female, 225 (90%) were Black (Black African or African Canadian), and median age was 52·0 years (IQR 48·0-56·0). 51 participants were enrolled in cohort 1, 50 in cohort 2, 50 in cohort 3, 50 in cohort 4, and 50 in cohort 5. 202 (80%) participants were assigned to receive rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP and 49 (20%) were assigned to receive placebo. One dose of rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP elicited superior immune responses compared with placebo, with GP-ELISA antibodies in the combined cohort (per-protocol population) increasing over 40-fold (GMTR 42·90, 95% CI 31·49-58·43; p<0·0001). In cohort 5, the GP-ELISA geometric mean titre 28 days after the second dose was over 200-fold higher in the rVSV-ZEBOV-GP group than in the placebo group (GMTR 208·66, 95% CI 115·57-376·72; p<0·0001). GFMI of PRNT titres was 11·51 (95% CI 9·82-13·50) at day 28 for participants in the combined cohort who received one dose of rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP and 86·64 (95% CI 69·85-107·46) 28 days after a second dose in cohort 5. Solicited adverse events up to 42 days after vaccination were mild to moderate in severity and transient. In the 14 days after the first dose of vaccine, the most common adverse events were injection site pain (130 of 201 participants, 65%), headache (109 of 201, 54%), fatigue (91 of 201, 45%), and joint pain (50 of 201, 25%). Unsolicited adverse events to day 42 were not different between participants who received rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP (103 of 201, 51%) and those who received placebo (22 of 49, 45%; p=0·52). No clinically significant changes in CD4 cell counts, HIV viral load, or haematological and biochemical laboratory tests were observed. INTERPRETATION: A single dose of rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP is highly immunogenic in people living with HIV on ART with an undetectable viral load, with a tolerable safety profile. A two-dose regimen in a subset of participating adolescents and adults showed a significant boosting at day 28, with no increase in reactogenicity compared with the first dose. FUNDING: International Development Research Centre, US Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response, Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, and the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness. TRANSLATION: For the French translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

papers.title: A participatory expert-based risk assessment to inform zoonotic disease surveillance in Cameroon: the case of Ebola virus disease and Rift Valley fever
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Viral haemorrhagic fevers (VHFs) are a group of zoonotic diseases caused by RNA viruses, including pathogens such as Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, and Rift Valley fever virus. Previous studies have identified Cameroon as a high-risk country, due to favourable ecoclimatic conditions and the presence of susceptible mammals and vectors that have been confirmed positive for viruses causing Rift Valley fever (RVF) and Ebola virus disease (EVD). Although evidence exists of RVF virus circulation in animals and serological reactivity to Ebola-related viruses among humans in Cameroon, the country has not officially documented epidemics of RVF or EVD. The objective of this study is to provide novel, context-refined knowledge of perceived risk factors and temporal patterns of RVF and EVD emergence in Cameroon, where epidemiological data on these two diseases are limited, with RVF explored through the livestock component and its early transmission dynamics in animal hosts, and zoonotic spillover to humans for EVD. Methods The present work proposes a risk assessment of RVF and EVD emergence through the development of a One Health integrated risk assessment tool for identifying perceived high-risk periods and key risk factors. A mixed, semi-quantitative approach involving expert semi-structured interviews, and a monthly calendar was used for data collection. Expert-based risk evaluation was then compared to risk factors derived from the scientific literature. Results For RVF, the wettest months seem to pose the highest risk, with increased inter-animal transmission during livestock transhumance. Key spatial determinants identified by experts included rainfall, host density, reservoirs, vectors, and livestock movements. For EVD spillover risk, human activities and behaviours, land cover, and host density were also perceived as critical. Convergences and divergences regarding expert-based and literature-based risk factors for RVF and EVD were observed, with variations concerning respectively livestock trade and socio-cultural practices linked to livelihood and forest-based subsistence. The distinction is likely attributable to the differing approaches of contextualization and generalization employed respectively by the two sources of weighting. Conclusions This study shows that, even in regions with no documented disease history, an integrated approach combining expert knowledge and literature-based evidence enables meaningful perceived risk assessment, generates novel and context-specific information, and supports the refinement of preventive strategies. The participatory visual tool introduced allows identification and quantification of putative zoonotic risk factors and their temporal dynamics, informing risk mapping, management, and communication.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limited epidemiological data on Ebola virus disease (EVD) and Rift Valley fever (RVF) in Cameroon by providing novel, context-refined knowledge of perceived risk factors and temporal patterns of their emergence.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study conducted a participatory expert-based risk assessment in Cameroon, focusing on the country's high-risk status due to its ecoclimatic conditions and the presence of susceptible mammals and vectors. The study involved expert semi-structured interviews and a monthly calendar to collect data on risk factors for RVF and EVD.
analysis.methods: A mixed, semi-quantitative approach was used, integrating expert semi-structured interviews and a monthly calendar for data collection. The study developed a One Health integrated risk assessment tool to identify perceived high-risk periods and key risk factors.
analysis.main_results: For RVF, the wettest months were identified as posing the highest risk, with increased inter-animal transmission during livestock transhumance. For EVD, human activities and behaviours, land cover, and host density were perceived as critical risk factors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that expert-based risk evaluation can generate novel and context-specific information, even in regions without documented disease history, by combining local knowledge with scientific literature.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the refinement of preventive strategies and risk mapping for zoonotic diseases in Cameroon, offering insights into the temporal dynamics of RVF and EVD emergence that can inform surveillance and management practices.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's reliance on expert opinion and semi-quantitative methods may limit the generalizability of findings, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the absence of direct empirical data on disease outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a participatory expert-based risk assessment to evaluate the emergence of Ebola virus disease (EVD) and Rift Valley fever (RVF) in Cameroon, where epidemiological data are limited. The research aimed to identify perceived risk factors and temporal patterns for both diseases, using a mixed, semi-quantitative approach involving expert interviews and a monthly calendar. For RVF, the wettest months were found to pose the highest risk, with increased transmission during livestock transhumance. For EVD, human activities, land cover, and host density were identified as critical factors. The study demonstrated that integrating expert knowledge with literature-based evidence can generate context-specific insights, even in regions without documented disease history. These findings have implications for improving surveillance and preventive strategies in Cameroon. However, the reliance on expert opinion and semi-quantitative methods may limit the generalizability of the results, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过提供关于感知风险因素及其出现时间模式的新颖、具体的知识,解决喀麦隆 埃博拉病毒病 (EVD) 和裂谷热 (RVF) 的有限流行病学数据问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究在喀麦隆进行了一项由专家参与的风险评估,重点关注该国由于其生态气候条件以及易感哺乳动物和 媒介 的存在而处于高风险状态。该研究涉及专家半结构化访谈和月度日历,以收集有关裂谷热和埃博拉病毒病风险因素的数据。
elements_zh.methods: 使用了混合的半定量方法,整合了专家半结构化访谈和数据收集的月度日历。该研究开发了一种 One Health 综合风险评估工具,以识别感知的高风险期和关键风险因素。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limited epidemiological data on Ebola virus disease (EVD) and Rift Valley fever (RVF) in Cameroon by providing novel, context-refined knowledge of perceived risk factors and temporal patterns of their emergence.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This study conducted a participatory expert-based risk assessment in Cameroon, focusing on the country's high-risk status due to its ecoclimatic conditions and the presence of susceptible mammals and vectors. The study involved expert semi-structured interviews and a monthly calendar to collect data on risk factors for RVF and EVD.
analysis_en.methods: A mixed, semi-quantitative approach was used, integrating expert semi-structured interviews and a monthly calendar for data collection. The study developed a One Health integrated risk assessment tool to identify perceived high-risk periods and key risk factors.
analysis_en.main_results: For RVF, the wettest months were identified as posing the highest risk, with increased inter-animal transmission during livestock transhumance. For EVD, human activities and behaviours, land cover, and host density were perceived as critical risk factors.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that expert-based risk evaluation can generate novel and context-specific information, even in regions without documented disease history, by combining local knowledge with scientific literature.

papers.title_zh: 一项基于专家参与的风险评估,旨在为喀麦隆的人畜共患疾病 监测 提供信息:埃博拉病毒病 和裂谷热的案例
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Viral haemorrhagic fevers (VHFs) are a group of zoonotic diseases caused by RNA viruses, including pathogens such as Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, and Rift Valley fever virus. Previous studies have identified Cameroon as a high-risk country, due to favourable ecoclimatic conditions and the presence of susceptible mammals and vectors that have been confirmed positive for viruses causing Rift Valley fever (RVF) and Ebola virus disease (EVD). Although evidence exists of RVF virus circulation in animals and serological reactivity to Ebola-related viruses among humans in Cameroon, the country has not officially documented epidemics of RVF or EVD. The objective of this study is to provide novel, context-refined knowledge of perceived risk factors and temporal patterns of RVF and EVD emergence in Cameroon, where epidemiological data on these two diseases are limited, with RVF explored through the livestock component and its early transmission dynamics in animal hosts, and zoonotic spillover to humans for EVD. Methods The present work proposes a risk assessment of RVF and EVD emergence through the development of a One Health integrated risk assessment tool for identifying perceived high-risk periods and key risk factors. A mixed, semi-quantitative approach involving expert semi-structured interviews, and a monthly calendar was used for data collection. Expert-based risk evaluation was then compared to risk factors derived from the scientific literature. Results For RVF, the wettest months seem to pose the highest risk, with increased inter-animal transmission during livestock transhumance. Key spatial determinants identified by experts included rainfall, host density, reservoirs, vectors, and livestock movements. For EVD spillover risk, human activities and behaviours, land cover, and host density were also perceived as critical. Convergences and divergences regarding expert-based and literature-based risk factors for RVF and EVD were observed, with variations concerning respectively livestock trade and socio-cultural practices linked to livelihood and forest-based subsistence. The distinction is likely attributable to the differing approaches of contextualization and generalization employed respectively by the two sources of weighting. Conclusions This study shows that, even in regions with no documented disease history, an integrated approach combining expert knowledge and literature-based evidence enables meaningful perceived risk assessment, generates novel and context-specific information, and supports the refinement of preventive strategies. The participatory visual tool introduced allows identification and quantification of putative zoonotic risk factors and their temporal dynamics, informing risk mapping, management, and communication.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景病毒性出血热(VHFs)是一组由RNA病毒引起的人畜共患疾病,病原体包括埃博拉病毒、马尔堡病毒、拉沙病毒、裂谷热病毒等。此前的研究已将喀麦隆确定为高风险国家,原因是其有利的生态气候条件以及易感哺乳动物和 媒介 的存在,这些哺乳动物和 媒介 已被证实对引起裂谷热 (RVF) 和 埃博拉病毒病 (EVD) 的病毒呈阳性。尽管有证据表明裂谷热病毒在喀麦隆动物中传播以及人类对埃博拉相关病毒有血清学反应,但该国尚未正式记录裂谷热或埃博拉病毒病的流行情况。本研究的目的是提供关于喀麦隆裂谷热和埃博拉病毒病出现的感知风险因素和时间模式的新颖、具体的知识,喀麦隆关于这两种疾病的流行病学数据有限,通过牲畜成分及其在动物宿主中的早期传播动态和人畜共患埃博拉病毒病中的人畜共患跨物种溢出来探索裂谷热。方法 目前的工作提出通过开发 One Health 综合风险评估工具来识别可感知的高风险期和关键风险因素,对裂谷热和埃博拉病毒病的出现进行风险评估。采用混合、半定量方法,包括专家半结构化访谈和月历来收集数据。然后将基于专家的风险评估与科学文献中得出的风险因素进行比较。结果 对于 RVF,最潮湿的月份似乎风险最高,牲畜迁移期间动物间的 传播 增加。专家确定的关键空间决定因素包括降雨量、宿主 密度、储存宿主、媒介 和牲畜迁徙。对于埃博拉病毒病 跨物种溢出 风险,人类活动和行为、土地覆盖和 宿主 密度也被认为至关重要。观察到基于专家和基于文献的裂谷热和埃博拉病毒病风险因素的趋同和分歧,分别与生计和森林生存相关的牲畜贸易和社会文化实践存在差异。这种区别可能归因于两种权重来源分别采用不同的情境化和概括方法。结论 这项研究表明,即使在没有疾病史记录的地区,结合专家知识和文献证据的综合方法也能实现有意义的感知风险评估,生成新颖且针对具体情况的信息,并支持完善预防策略。引入的参与式视觉工具可以识别和量化假定的人畜共患风险因素及其时间动态,为风险绘图、管理和沟通提供信息。

papers.title: Bundibugyo virus disease: transmission dynamics, infectiousness and viral persistence.
papers.abstract: BVD is a severe filoviral haemorrhagic fever caused by the Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), for which outbreak-related evidence remains limited compared with that available for Zaire ebolavirus. This perspective summarizes current evidence on transmission dynamics, presymptomatic infectiousness, post-recovery viral persistence and the duration of infectiousness, distinguishing BDBV-specific data from evidence extrapolated from other ortho-Ebolaviruses. Available epidemiological data from the 2007-2008 outbreak in Uganda indicate that BDBV transmission occurs primarily through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of symptomatic or deceased individuals, with the handling of corpses representing a significant risk factor (adjusted odds ratio 3.83; 95% confidence interval 1.78-8.23). The average incubation period is 6.3 days, and prolonged chains of transmission were documented in household and healthcare settings. No documented human cases of pre-symptomatic transmission have been reported, however, the limited number of documented outbreaks precludes excluding this possibility, and experimental animal data support its biological plausibility. No BDBV-specific data are available regarding viral persistence and duration of infectiousness. Consequently, current recommendations rely largely on evidence derived from other orthoebolaviruses. Viral RNA may persist after recovery in immunoprivileged sites, particularly in semen, with rare but documented episodes of delayed transmission. The ongoing outbreak highlights the need for BDBV-specific studies to strengthen the evidence base underpinning public health recommendations.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), a severe filoviral haemorrhagic fever caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), focusing on transmission dynamics, presymptomatic infectiousness, post-recovery viral persistence, and duration of infectiousness, with a central question on BDBV-specific evidence versus extrapolated data from other orthoebolaviruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This perspective synthesizes current evidence on BDBV, distinguishing BDBV-specific data from extrapolated evidence from other orthoebolaviruses, and reports that outbreak-related evidence for BVD remains limited compared with Zaire ebolavirus.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Epidemiological data from the 2007-2008 Uganda outbreak indicate that BDBV transmission occurs primarily through direct contact with blood or body fluids of symptomatic or deceased individuals, with corpse handling as a significant risk factor (adjusted odds ratio 3.83; 95% CI 1.78-8.23). The average incubation period is 6.3 days, and prolonged transmission chains were documented in household and healthcare settings.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: No documented human cases of presymptomatic transmission have been reported for BDBV, though the limited number of documented outbreaks precludes excluding this possibility, and experimental animal data suggest biological plausibility. Additionally, no BDBV-specific data exist regarding viral persistence and duration of infectiousness, with current recommendations relying largely on evidence from other orthoebolaviruses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the urgent need for BDBV-specific studies to strengthen the evidence base underpinning public health recommendations, particularly regarding presymptomatic transmission, viral persistence, and duration of infectiousness.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), a severe filoviral haemorrhagic fever caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). It synthesizes current evidence on transmission dynamics, presymptomatic infectiousness, and post-recovery viral persistence, emphasizing BDBV-specific data versus extrapolated evidence from other orthoebolaviruses. Key findings include primary transmission through direct contact with symptomatic or deceased individuals, with corpse handling as a significant risk factor (aOR 3.83; 95% CI 1.78-8.23), an average incubation period of 6.3 days, and prolonged transmission chains in household and healthcare settings. However, no human cases of presymptomatic transmission have been documented, and BDBV-specific data on viral persistence and infectiousness duration are lacking, with recommendations currently relying on evidence from other orthoebolaviruses. The review underscores the critical need for BDBV-specific research to inform public health measures.

papers.source_body_en: BVD is a severe filoviral haemorrhagic fever caused by the Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), for which outbreak-related evidence remains limited compared with that available for Zaire ebolavirus. This perspective summarizes current evidence on transmission dynamics, presymptomatic infectiousness, post-recovery viral persistence and the duration of infectiousness, distinguishing BDBV-specific data from evidence extrapolated from other ortho-Ebolaviruses. Available epidemiological data from the 2007-2008 outbreak in Uganda indicate that BDBV transmission occurs primarily through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of symptomatic or deceased individuals, with the handling of corpses representing a significant risk factor (adjusted odds ratio 3.83; 95% confidence interval 1.78-8.23). The average incubation period is 6.3 days, and prolonged chains of transmission were documented in household and healthcare settings. No documented human cases of pre-symptomatic transmission have been reported, however, the limited number of documented outbreaks precludes excluding this possibility, and experimental animal data support its biological plausibility. No BDBV-specific data are available regarding viral persistence and duration of infectiousness. Consequently, current recommendations rely largely on evidence derived from other orthoebolaviruses. Viral RNA may persist after recovery in immunoprivileged sites, particularly in semen, with rare but documented episodes of delayed transmission. The ongoing outbreak highlights the need for BDBV-specific studies to strengthen the evidence base underpinning public health recommendations.

papers.title: Pan-Ebolavirus nanoparticle vaccine provides protection in rodents from lethal infection by Zaire and Sudan viruses
papers.abstract: Abstract Both Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) and Sudan ebolavirus (SUDV) are members of the genus Ebolavirus and cause outbreaks marked by high fatality rates and repeated spillover from animal reservoirs. Filoviral glycoproteins (GPs) are the primary targets of neutralizing antibodies and form the basis of current vaccines. Here we describe the design, structural characterization, and evaluation of two-component self-assembling icosahedral I53-50 nanoparticles displaying prefusion EBOV or SUDV GP antigens, either individually or in cocktail and mosaic multivalent formats. EBOV-GP-I53-50 and SUDV-GP-I53-50 nanoparticles elicited strong homologous protection in mice and guinea pigs. In the mouse-adapted EBOV model (maEBOV), mosaic and cocktail formulations produced weak survival below that of the matched EBOV-GP-I53-50 GP immunogen. In contrast, in the gpaSUDV guinea pig model (gpSUDV), cocktail and mosaic nanoparticles elicited robust protection against gpSUDV, and detectable antibody responses to both SUDV and EBOV GPs. These findings demonstrate that multivalent GP-I53-50 nanoparticle immunogens can protect rodents from death, severe clinical signs of disease, and weight loss in relevant models. Together with the established clinical safety of the I53-50 platform, these results support continued efforts toward the development of a pan-ebolavirus vaccine.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) and Sudan ebolavirus (SUDV) cause outbreaks with high fatality rates and repeated spillover from animal reservoirs, highlighting the need for broadly protective vaccines. The study addresses whether multivalent nanoparticle immunogens displaying EBOV and SUDV glycoproteins can elicit protective immunity against lethal infection in relevant animal models.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated two-component self-assembling icosahedral I53-50 nanoparticles displaying prefusion EBOV or SUDV GP antigens, either individually, in cocktail, or mosaic multivalent formats. Protection was assessed in mouse-adapted EBOV (maEBOV) and guinea pig-adapted SUDV (gpSUDV) models.
analysis.methods: Nanoparticles were designed, structurally characterized, and evaluated for immunogenicity and protection in rodents. The study reports survival, clinical signs, and weight loss outcomes following lethal challenge with maEBOV or gpSUDV.
analysis.main_results: EBOV-GP-I53-50 and SUDV-GP-I53-50 nanoparticles elicited strong homologous protection in mice and guinea pigs. In the maEBOV model, mosaic and cocktail formulations produced weak survival below that of the matched EBOV-GP-I53-50 immunogen. In the gpSUDV model, cocktail and mosaic nanoparticles elicited robust protection against gpSUDV and detectable antibody responses to both SUDV and EBOV GPs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that multivalent GP-I53-50 nanoparticle immunogens can protect rodents from death, severe clinical signs, and weight loss in relevant models. The study highlights the potential of mosaic and cocktail nanoparticle vaccines as a strategy for pan-ebolavirus protection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results support continued development of a pan-ebolavirus vaccine, leveraging the established clinical safety of the I53-50 platform. The findings suggest a path toward broader protection against multiple ebolaviruses, addressing a critical unmet need in outbreak response.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to rodent models and does not assess human immunogenicity or efficacy. While the I53-50 platform has clinical safety data, translation to humans requires further evaluation. The evidence is moderate due to the preclinical nature and model-specific findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study designed and evaluated two-component icosahedral I53-50 nanoparticles displaying prefusion glycoproteins from Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) and Sudan ebolavirus (SUDV), including individual, cocktail, and mosaic multivalent formats. In rodent models, EBOV-GP-I53-50 and SUDV-GP-I53-50 nanoparticles elicited strong homologous protection, while mosaic and cocktail formulations showed variable efficacy depending on the challenge model. In the mouse-adapted EBOV model, mosaic and cocktail formulations underperformed compared to the matched EBOV-GP-I53-50 immunogen, whereas in the guinea pig-adapted SUDV model, both cocktail and mosaic nanoparticles provided robust protection and induced detectable cross-reactive antibody responses. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that multivalent nanoparticle immunogens can protect against lethal infection and severe disease in relevant animal models, supporting the development of a pan-ebolavirus vaccine. The study’s clinical relevance is supported by the established safety of the I53-50 platform, though translation to humans remains untested. Limitations include the preclinical nature of the work, reliance on rodent models, and lack of human immunogenicity data, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) and Sudan ebolavirus (SUDV) cause outbreaks with high fatality rates and repeated spillover from animal reservoirs, highlighting the need for broadly protective vaccines. The study addresses whether multivalent nanoparticle immunogens displaying EBOV and SUDV glycoproteins can elicit protective immunity against lethal infection in relevant animal models.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated two-component self-assembling icosahedral I53-50 nanoparticles displaying prefusion EBOV or SUDV GP antigens, either individually, in cocktail, or mosaic multivalent formats. Protection was assessed in mouse-adapted EBOV (maEBOV) and guinea pig-adapted SUDV (gpSUDV) models.
analysis_en.methods: Nanoparticles were designed, structurally characterized, and evaluated for immunogenicity and protection in rodents. The study reports survival, clinical signs, and weight loss outcomes following lethal challenge with maEBOV or gpSUDV.
analysis_en.main_results: EBOV-GP-I53-50 and SUDV-GP-I53-50 nanoparticles elicited strong homologous protection in mice and guinea pigs. In the maEBOV model, mosaic and cocktail formulations produced weak survival below that of the matched EBOV-GP-I53-50 immunogen. In the gpSUDV model, cocktail and mosaic nanoparticles elicited robust protection against gpSUDV and detectable antibody responses to both SUDV and EBOV GPs.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that multivalent GP-I53-50 nanoparticle immunogens can protect rodents from death, severe clinical signs, and weight loss in relevant models. The study highlights the potential of mosaic and cocktail nanoparticle vaccines as a strategy for pan-ebolavirus protection.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results support continued development of a pan-ebolavirus vaccine, leveraging the established clinical safety of the I53-50 platform. The findings suggest a path toward broader protection against multiple ebolaviruses, addressing a critical unmet need in outbreak response.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to rodent models and does not assess human immunogenicity or efficacy. While the I53-50 platform has clinical safety data, translation to humans requires further evaluation. The evidence is moderate due to the preclinical nature and model-specific findings.

papers.title_zh: 泛埃博拉病毒纳米颗粒 疫苗 可以保护啮齿动物免受扎伊尔病毒和苏丹病毒的致命感染
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Both Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) and Sudan ebolavirus (SUDV) are members of the genus Ebolavirus and cause outbreaks marked by high fatality rates and repeated spillover from animal reservoirs. Filoviral glycoproteins (GPs) are the primary targets of neutralizing antibodies and form the basis of current vaccines. Here we describe the design, structural characterization, and evaluation of two-component self-assembling icosahedral I53-50 nanoparticles displaying prefusion EBOV or SUDV GP antigens, either individually or in cocktail and mosaic multivalent formats. EBOV-GP-I53-50 and SUDV-GP-I53-50 nanoparticles elicited strong homologous protection in mice and guinea pigs. In the mouse-adapted EBOV model (maEBOV), mosaic and cocktail formulations produced weak survival below that of the matched EBOV-GP-I53-50 GP immunogen. In contrast, in the gpaSUDV guinea pig model (gpSUDV), cocktail and mosaic nanoparticles elicited robust protection against gpSUDV, and detectable antibody responses to both SUDV and EBOV GPs. These findings demonstrate that multivalent GP-I53-50 nanoparticle immunogens can protect rodents from death, severe clinical signs of disease, and weight loss in relevant models. Together with the established clinical safety of the I53-50 platform, these results support continued efforts toward the development of a pan-ebolavirus vaccine.

papers.full_text: Abstract Background Urban outbreaks of Ebola present heightened risks of rapid amplification and cross-regional spread. On 30 January 2025, the Uganda Ministry of Health declared an Ebola Sudan virus disease (SVD) outbreak first identified in a fatal case at a national referral hospital in Kampala, one of East Africa’s most densely populated and highly connected urban centres. The source of the index infection, presumed to be a zoonotic spillover event, was not established. Despite high transmission risk and major disruptions in global health financing, the outbreak was rapidly contained. We analysed the response to identify innovations and system adaptations that enabled control and to derive lessons for future preparedness in resource-constrained settings. Methods We conducted a retrospective implementation analysis using a structured review of national and district response plans, situation reports, laboratory and surveillance summaries, early and after-action review reports, policies, and standard operating procedures generated during the 2025 SVD response. Data were analysed using a framework-based thematic analysis organised around the World Health Organization (WHO) Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) response pillars, to identify innovations and intensified adaptations of existing approaches. Results The outbreak was limited to 14 cases (12 confirmed, 2 probable) across seven districts, with two deaths among confirmed cases (confirmed-case fatality rate 16.7% (2/12; 95% CI 4.7–44.8)) and all confirmed cases admitted to Ebola Treatment Units survived. Key implementation innovations included institutional quarantine of all identified contacts; decentralisation and early deployment of mobile laboratory services and district laboratory response teams; rapid deployment of candidate therapeutics and vaccines through pre-approved research readiness platforms; use of a real-time digital 4 W (who, what, where, and when) coordination and partner mapping dashboard; and intensified mortality surveillance linked to rapid laboratory confirmation. Despite mobilising only 29% of the estimated response budget (USD 16 million of an estimated USD 56 million required), coordinated resource allocation enabled rapid interruption of transmission. Conclusion Preparedness investments, aggressive contact containment, intensified mortality surveillance, research readiness, and digital coordination enabled rapid control of an urban SVD outbreak in a resource-constrained setting. These findings support institutionalising mortality-led surveillance, domestic emergency financing, research readiness, and establishing institutional quarantine of contacts as default policy for filovirus outbreaks in dense urban settings. Funding No funding was obtained. Ethics declarations Ethics Approval and Consent to Participate Ethics approval was not required for this study and was therefore not obtained. This work is a retrospective implementation analysis of the 2025 SVD outbreak detection and response in Uganda, conducted as part of public health practice and after-action learning. It relied exclusively on aggregated operational documents generated during the outbreak response and shared by the Uganda Ministry of Health and the World Health Organization Country Office for Uganda. No primary data were collected from human participants, and no identifiable individual-level patient data, clinical records, or biological specimens were accessed or analysed. Accordingly, the requirement for informed consent was not applicable. On this basis, the work was classified as non-research public health practice rather than human-subjects research and did not require review or approval by a research ethics committee, consistent with national research-ethics guidance in Uganda. analysis.research_question_and_background: Urban Ebola Sudan virus disease (SVD) outbreaks pose exceptional risks of rapid amplification and cross-regional spread, yet the 2025 Kampala outbreak was contained despite high transmission risk and constrained financing. The study aimed to identify innovations and system adaptations that enabled rapid control and to derive lessons for future preparedness in resource-constrained settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective implementation analysis examined the 2025 SVD outbreak response in Uganda, relying on aggregated operational documents from the Ministry of Health and WHO Country Office. The outbreak was first identified in Kampala on 30 January 2025 and involved 14 cases across seven districts.
analysis.methods: A framework-based thematic analysis was applied to national and district response plans, situation reports, laboratory and surveillance summaries, after-action reviews, policies, and standard operating procedures using the WHO Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan pillars. No primary data were collected from human participants, and no identifiable individual-level patient data were accessed.
analysis.main_results: The outbreak comprised 14 cases (12 confirmed, 2 probable) with two deaths among confirmed cases (confirmed-case fatality rate 16.7% (2/12; 95% CI 4.7–44.8)), and all confirmed cases admitted to Ebola Treatment Units survived. Key innovations included institutional quarantine of contacts, decentralised mobile laboratories, rapid deployment of therapeutics and vaccines via pre-approved research platforms, a real-time 4W coordination dashboard, and intensified mortality surveillance.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that preparedness investments, aggressive contact containment, intensified mortality surveillance, research readiness, and digital coordination enabled rapid interruption of transmission in an urban SVD outbreak. They highlight the novelty of institutionalising mortality-led surveillance, domestic emergency financing, research readiness, and institutional quarantine of contacts as default policy for filovirus outbreaks in dense urban settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: They also underscore the value of coordinated resource allocation even with limited budgets for rapid outbreak control.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, reliance on aggregated operational documents, and lack of primary patient-level data, which constrains causal inference and generalisability. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these methodological constraints and the absence of formal controls.

analysis.summary_en: This study retrospectively analysed the 2025 Sudan virus disease (SVD) outbreak response in Kampala, Uganda, to identify innovations enabling rapid containment despite high urban transmission risk and constrained financing. Using a framework-based thematic analysis of operational documents, the authors found that 14 cases occurred across seven districts with a confirmed-case fatality rate of 16.7% and no deaths among treated patients. Key innovations included institutional quarantine of contacts, decentralised mobile laboratories, rapid deployment of therapeutics and vaccines via pre-approved research platforms, a real-time 4W coordination dashboard, and intensified mortality surveillance. The authors conclude that preparedness investments, aggressive contact containment, intensified mortality surveillance, research readiness, and digital coordination enabled rapid interruption of transmission. They recommend institutionalising mortality-led surveillance, domestic emergency financing, research readiness, and institutional quarantine of contacts as default policy for filovirus outbreaks in dense urban settings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the retrospective design, reliance on aggregated documents, and absence of primary patient-level data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 城市埃博拉苏丹病毒病 (SVD) 暴发 带来快速放大和跨区域传播的特殊风险,但 2025 年坎帕拉 暴发 尽管 传播 风险高且融资有限,但仍得到了遏制。该研究旨在确定能够实现快速控制的创新和系统调整,并为资源有限环境中的未来准备工作吸取经验教训。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性实施分析依据卫生部和世卫组织国家办事处的汇总业务文件,审查了乌干达 2025 年 SVD 暴发 的应对措施。暴发 于 2025 年 1 月 30 日在坎帕拉首次发现,涉及七个地区的 14 例病例。
elements_zh.methods: 使用世卫组织战略准备和应对计划支柱,将基于框架的主题分析应用于国家和地区应对计划、情况报告、实验室和 监测 摘要、行动后审查、政策和标准操作程序。没有从人类参与者那里收集主要数据,也没有访问可识别的个人患者数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 暴发 包括 14 例(12 例确诊,2 例疑似),确诊病例中有 2 例死亡(确诊病例死亡率 16.7%(2/12;95% CI 4.7–44.8)),埃博拉 治疗 病房收治的所有确诊病例均存活。主要创新包括对接触者进行机构隔离、分散的移动实验室、通过预先批准的研究平台快速部署治疗方法和 疫苗、实时 4W 协调仪表板以及强化的 死亡率 监测。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,准备投资、积极的接触遏制、强化的 死亡率 监测、研究准备和数字协调使得 传播 在城市 SVD 暴发 中迅速中断。他们强调了将 死亡率 主导的 监测 制度化、国内紧急融资、研究准备和接触者机构隔离作为密集城市环境中丝状病毒 暴发 的默认政策的新颖性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 他们还强调了协调资源分配的价值,即使预算有限,也能实现快速 暴发 控制。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计、对汇总操作文件的依赖以及缺乏主要患者数据而受到限制,从而限制了因果推断和普遍性。由于这些方法学限制和缺乏正式控制,证据强度被评估为中等。

Methods We conducted a retrospective implementation analysis using a structured review of national and district response plans, situation reports, laboratory and surveillance summaries, early and after-action review reports, policies, and standard operating procedures generated during the 2025 SVD response. papers.title: Reopening the discussion on Ebola virus nomenclature in the context of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak
papers.abstract: In May 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) declared the ongoing Ebola virus outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo species in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern and a public health emergency of continental security, respectively [1, 2]. These declarations are intended to mobilise global attention, trigger international support and funding, encourage timely recommendations for trade and travel, and strengthen surveillance and response measures. During such periods, the public frequently seeks clarification and opinions from experts. In my experience as an infectious disease epidemiologist, the name “Bundibugyo”, which is actually a district in Uganda where the virus species was first identified, generated fear and panic during the first days of the outbreak, with many people questioning whether Bundibugyo District is affected and should be avoided, or whether travel to Uganda should be restricted altogether [3]. Such perceptions may adversely affect tourism, travel, trade, and local economies, and contribute to the social exclusion of some communities, as observed in previous outbreaks [4]. Bundibugyo is a major tourist destination, and with the summer months approaching, this could pose a danger to tourism in Uganda following travel notices released by, for example, the United States government. Consequently, these implications may further complicate outbreak preparedness and response due to the sensitivity they create. Historically, ebolavirus species were named after geographical locations where they were first identified, a convention that reflected prevailing virological naming practices at the time [5]. However, advances in understanding the social consequences of disease naming have led to greater emphasis on nomenclature that preserves scientific precision [6]. A previous article by Olupot-Olupot and colleagues called for a stigma-free and scientifically precise Ebola virus nomenclature, highlighting the need to minimise the potential harm associated with disease names [7]. They argued that the nomenclature of several ebolavirus species, including Zaire ebolavirus, Sudan ebolavirus, and Bundibugyo ebolavirus, may unintentionally create negative perceptions because these names are directly linked to geographic locations. This call needs to be reignited to establish proper nomenclature for these viruses, or at the very least to ensure alignment during outbreaks. WHO’s best practices for naming infectious diseases discourage the use of geographic references and terminology that may promote discrimination or segregation [6]. Similar principles informed the transition from Mpox during the global outbreak in 2022 [8]. In light of these considerations, scientists, alongside affected communities, public health institutions such as WHO and Africa CDC, and international taxonomy bodies such as the International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses, should initiate and/or be involved in renewed dialogue and evidence-based consultations to help align Ebola virus nomenclature with contemporary principles of equity and non-stigmatising communication. While any future changes would require consideration of implications for surveillance systems, laboratory reporting, and international classification frameworks, these challenges should not discourage evidence-informed discussion of whether current nomenclature remains fit for purpose.
papers.journal: Journal of Interventional Epidemiology and Public Health

papers.title_original: Emergence of a Bundibugyo virus variant in the 2026 outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the emergence of a Bundibugyo virus variant during the 2026 outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, highlighting a knowledge gap regarding the genomic and epidemiological characteristics of this variant and its implications for outbreak response.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted a genomic and epidemiological investigation of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus outbreak, analyzing clinical samples and epidemiological data from affected regions in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.
analysis.methods: Whole-genome sequencing was performed on clinical samples from confirmed cases, followed by phylogenetic and comparative genomic analyses to characterize the variant and trace its transmission dynamics. Epidemiological data were collected to assess outbreak spread and risk factors.
analysis.main_results: Genomic analysis identified a novel Bundibugyo virus variant with distinct mutations compared to historical strains, and phylogenetic reconstruction showed sustained human-to-human transmission within and between the two countries during the 2026 outbreak.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence of a rapidly evolving Bundibugyo virus variant capable of sustained transmission, representing a novel public health challenge distinct from prior outbreaks. The study provides the first detailed genomic characterization of this variant in the context of a cross-border outbreak.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the need for enhanced genomic surveillance and rapid response strategies to detect and contain emerging Bundibugyo virus variants, particularly in regions with overlapping outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a subset of available clinical samples and the absence of experimental validation of the variant's phenotypic properties, warranting cautious interpretation of the transmission dynamics and public health implications.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the emergence of a Bundibugyo virus variant during the 2026 outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. Using whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis of clinical samples, researchers identified a novel variant with distinct mutations and evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission across borders. The authors interpret these findings as indicative of a rapidly evolving virus capable of sustained spread, representing a new public health challenge. The work highlights the importance of genomic surveillance and rapid response to detect and contain emerging variants, though limitations include reliance on a subset of samples and lack of experimental validation of phenotypic changes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究讨论了 2026 年 暴发 期间在刚果民主共和国和乌干达出现的本迪布焦病毒变种,强调了有关该变种的基因组和流行病学特征及其对 暴发 应对的影响的知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究对2026年本迪布焦病毒暴发进行了基因组和流行病学调查,分析了刚果民主共和国和乌干达受影响地区的临床样本和流行病学数据。
elements_zh.methods: 对确诊病例的临床样本进行全 基因组 测序,然后进行系统发育和比较基因组分析,以表征变异并追踪其 传播 动态。收集流行病学数据以评估 暴发 的传播和危险因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 基因组分析发现了一种新的本迪布焦病毒变种,与历史毒株相比具有独特的 传播,系统发育重建显示 2026 年 暴发 期间两国内部和之间持续存在人与人之间的 传播。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为快速进化的本迪布焦病毒变种能够持续 传播 的证据,代表着与之前的 暴发 不同的新的公共卫生挑战。该研究首次在跨境 暴发 背景下详细描述了该变体的基因组特征。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调需要增强 基因组监测 和快速响应策略来检测和遏制新出现的本迪布焦病毒变种,特别是在 基因组监测 重叠的区域。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其依赖于可用临床样本的子集,并且缺乏对该变体表型特性的实验验证,因此需要对 传播 动态和公共卫生影响进行谨慎解释。

papers.title: An imported case of Bundibugyo virus infection, France, June 2026
papers.abstract: In June 2026, an intensive care physician deployed in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and previously vaccinated against Ebola virus developed fatigue, nausea and headaches while returning to France. Bundibugyo virus was identified with RT-PCR. The patient was treated with remdesivir and recovered fully. Contact tracing identified five low-risk contacts and no secondary cases. Stringent infection prevention and control measures and multidisciplinary collaboration are important when managing suspected or confirmed Ebola disease cases, even with low viral loads.

Bundibugyo virus was identified with RT-PCR. The patient was treated with remdesivir and recovered fully. Contact tracing identified five low-risk contacts and no secondary cases. Stringent infection prevention and control measures and multidisciplinary collaboration are important when managing suspected or confirmed Ebola disease cases, even with low viral loads.
